title: Joggins Fossil Cliffs: Carboniferous coal forests and early reptiles
summary: The Joggins cliffs on the Nova Scotia coast expose Pennsylvanian "Coal Age" strata about 318–303 million years old, with upright fossil trees, tracks and the remains of early animals. UNESCO counts 96 genera and 148 species from three ecosystems: an estuarine bay, a floodplain rainforest and a fire-prone forested plain. The site is known for the earliest reptiles, such as Hylonomus lyelli.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO dates the Pennsylvanian strata to 318–303 million years ago.

as_recorded.value: the Pennsylvanian strata (dating back 318 to 303 million years)
